statement:
The exact cohomological dimensions and the real exception — Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated of transcendence degree $n$, let
$k$ be the algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$ in $K$, and put
$P=G_{K\overline k}$ and $E=G_K$. With continuous cohomology of discrete
torsion modules,
\[
 \operatorname{cd}_\ell P=n\quad\hbox{for every prime }\ell,
 \qquad \operatorname{cd}P=n,
\]
\[
 \operatorname{cd}_\ell E=n+2\quad(\ell\ne2),\qquad
 \operatorname{cd}_2E=
 \begin{cases}n+2&K\text{ not formally real},\\
 \infty&K\text{ formally real}.
 \end{cases}
\]
In every case $\operatorname{vcd}_2E=\operatorname{cd}_2G_{K(i)}=n+2$.
Thus the equalities proposed in F1 hold, with precisely this exception
at two (149, section 1, manuscript p.~6, scan 13). For a general
function field, the relevant condition is an ordering of $K$ itself,
not just a real embedding of its constant number field.
depends_on: Milne LEC Theorem 15.2; Milne ADT I.2.1, I.4.10(c), I.4.16; Serre 1965 section 1; A2
notes: F1. The real exception concerns formal reality of K, not only real places of its constant number field.

statement:
Finite-order elements and complex conjugation — For a field $F$ of characteristic zero, every nonidentity element of finite
order in $G_F=\operatorname{Gal}(F^{\rm sep}/F)$ has order two. Its centralizer
is the subgroup of order two that it generates. In $G_{\mathbb Q}$ all such
elements are conjugate to the complex conjugation determined by
$\overline{\mathbb Q}\subset\mathbb C$. Every open subgroup of
$G_{\mathbb Q}$ has trivial centralizer in $G_{\mathbb Q}$.
This answers F2 (149, section 1, manuscript p.~6, scan 14).
depends_on: Geyer section 3 Example 2 and section 4 Theorem 1; Minamide–Tsujimura, 15 February 2022, Theorem 2.7 and Proposition 1.2
notes: F2. The attached return B2 was checked; its conclusion is independently sourced here.

statement:
Open subgroups, torsion, and centers of profinite surface groups — Let $P$ be the full profinite completion of either a free group of finite
rank $r\geq2$, or the fundamental group of a closed oriented surface of
genus $g\geq2$. Every open subgroup has trivial centralizer in $P$, and
$P$ has no nonidentity element of finite order. An open subgroup of index
$d$ is the full profinite completion of a free group of rank
$1+d(r-1)$, respectively a surface group of genus $1+d(g-1)$.
The free rank-one exception is $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$, whose center and the
centralizers of all its open subgroups equal the whole group.
These statements answer F3 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~7 and 13,
scans 15 and 28).
depends_on: Nakamura Corollary 1.3.4; Mochizuki–Tamagawa Proposition 1.4 and Remarks 1.1.5, 1.2.2; explicit covering/character argument
notes: F3. Includes full profinite free and compact surface groups; rank one and the four nonhyperbolic curve types are explicit.

statement:
Inertia at distinct lifted cusps — Let $C$ be a smooth connected curve over an algebraically closed field of
characteristic zero, of hyperbolic type $(g,r)$ with $r>0$, and let
$P=\pi_1(C)$. In the normalization of its smooth compactification in the
universal pro-\'etale cover, each cusp $c$ has inertia
$I_c\simeq\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)$. Distinct lifted cusps have
$I_c\cap I_d=1$. Moreover
\[
 N_P(I_c)=I_c,\qquad C_P(H)=I_c\quad(1\ne H\subset I_c).
\]
Here subgroups are actual chosen subgroups; changing the universal lift
conjugates all statements simultaneously. This supplies the loop inputs
requested with F3.
depends_on: A3; surface meridian presentation; Mochizuki Lemma 1.3.7
manuscript_passages: cote 149; section 1; pp. 7, 13; scans 15, 28; loop inputs required in Part A
notes: F3 ancillary assertion. Actual subgroups use compatible lifted cusps. Proves trivial intersection, self-normalization and centralizers of nontrivial inertia subgroups.

statement:
Extensions and inverse limits — The property $C_P(H)=1$ for every open subgroup $H\subset P$ passes to
extensions of profinite groups and to directed inverse limits with
surjective transition maps. Consequently every successive extension of
nonabelian free profinite groups and profinite hyperbolic surface groups
has this property. The limit statement fills the omission between scans
12 and 15 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~5--7).
depends_on: A3; finite étale descent on dense opens
notes: F3. Surjective projections are supplied, including the actual field inverse-limit maps.

statement:
Theorem 1 and its strengthening — Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated, let $k$ be the algebraic closure
of $\mathbb Q$ in $K$, and fix an algebraic closure $\overline K$ with
$\overline k\subset\overline K$. Put
$E=G_K$ and $P=G_{K\overline k}$. Every open subgroup of $E$, respectively
$P$, has trivial centralizer in $E$, respectively $P$. For
$\operatorname{trdeg}(K/k)>0$ one has, more strongly,
\[
 C_E(H)=1\quad\text{for every open }H\subset P,
 \qquad G_k\longrightarrow\operatorname{Out}(P)\text{ is injective}.
\]
This is Theorem 1 and the Remarque (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~6 and
10, scans 13 and 21; F4).
depends_on: A1–A5; Geyer section 4 Theorem 2; Minamide–Tsujimura Theorem 2.7 and Proposition 1.2; Hoshi–Mochizuki Theorem C(ii)
notes: F4. The maps G_(K kbar) -> G_(F kbar) -> pi1(U_kbar) are continuous surjective and outer-equivariant. The centralizer strengthening requires positive transcendence degree.

statement:
The rational-point group of a semiabelian variety — Let $K$ be finitely generated over its prime field and let
$1\to T\to G\to A\to1$ be a semiabelian variety over $K$.
As an abstract abelian group $G(K)$ is a direct sum of a finite group and
a free abelian group, whose rank can be infinite. Consequently
\[
 \bigcap_{n\geq1}nG(K)=0.
\]
In characteristic $p>0$ the exact prime-to-$p$ variant is
\[
 \bigcap_{(n,p)=1}nG(K)=G(K)[p^\infty].
\]
The finite-generation assertion on scan 34 is false: already
$\mathbb G_m(\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q^*$ has one independent generator for
each rational prime. This answers the erroneous input of F6 (149,
section 1, manuscript p.~16, scan 34).
depends_on: Divisors on normal proper models; Milne ANT Theorem 5.1; Milne AV Theorem 16.7
notes: F6. G(K) is finite torsion plus free abelian, possibly of infinite rank. Q* refutes finite generation.

statement:
Kummer comparison and Theorem 3 in characteristic zero — Let $K/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated, let $X/K$ be geometrically
connected of finite type, and let $i:X\hookrightarrow G$ be an immersion
into a semiabelian variety. Both maps (*) and (**) on scans 32--33 are
injective: $K$-points have distinct geometric conjugacy classes of
sections, already after abelianizing the geometric kernel. This is
Theorem 3 in its stated embedding generality (149, section 1, manuscript
pp.~15--17, scans 32--35; F6).
depends_on: B1; Kummer exact sequences; compactness of compatible finite division-point sets
notes: F6. Corrects finite generation while proving Theorem 3 in the actual semiabelian-immersion generality. Kernel on omitted primes is precisely omitted-primary torsion.

statement:
Corollary 1(a), with the translation in the correct group — Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X$ be a reduced connected
finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $f,g:X\to Y$ be morphisms, where
$i:Y\hookrightarrow G$ is an immersion into a semiabelian variety.
For any prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, equality
$H_1(f,\mathbb Z_\ell)=H_1(g,\mathbb Z_\ell)$ implies a unique
$a\in G(k)$ with $i\circ g=\tau_a\circ i\circ f$.
This proves Corollary 1(a), including its one-prime refinement, on
scans 24--25 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~11--12; F5).
The printed/transcribed $a\in Y$ must be corrected to $a\in G$:
with $Y=\mathbb G_m\setminus\{1\}$ and $f=g$, the difference is
$1\notin Y$.
depends_on: Milne AV III.6.1, III.9.1, III.9.6; explicit curve reduction and torus meridians
notes: F5 Corollary 1(a). Correct translation parameter belongs to G(k). Works in arbitrary characteristic with one invertible prime.

statement:
The open-subset translation lemma and its exact curve correction — The lemma of scan 37 is false for the hyperbolic type $(1,1)$.
For a smooth hyperbolic curve $Y=C\setminus D$ over an algebraically
closed field, with its generalized Abel map $\alpha:Y\hookrightarrow J_D^1$,
the following is the exact correction on curve types: a translation
sending a nonempty open of $\alpha(Y)$ into $\alpha(Y)$ is trivial for
every hyperbolic type except $(1,1)$; for type $(1,1)$ every translation
has that property. Full setwise stability $\alpha(Y)+u=\alpha(Y)$ forces
$u=0$ in every hyperbolic type. Here the field has characteristic zero;
the same proof uses prime-to-characteristic cohomology in arbitrary
characteristic. This answers the lemma and the homological proof in F5
(149, section 1, manuscript pp.~18--19, scans 37--40).
depends_on: B3; generalized Abel homology; meridian coordinate spans; Riemann–Hurwitz; AB_checks.py
notes: F5 lemma false in type (1,1); complete curve-type correction and full-stability theorem proved. The exact failure in scans39–40 persists under shrinking.

statement:
Corollaries 1(b), 2(c)--(d), and 3 with all comparison maps — A hyperbolic polycurve means a finite tower of smooth pairs whose
geometric curve fibres have $2g-2+r>0$, including proper fibres.
Over a field finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$, rational points
of a hyperbolic polycurve have distinct geometric conjugacy classes
of full point sections, and a point section has trivial centralizer
in the geometric group. For a reduced geometrically connected
finite-type source, the arithmetic outer fundamental-group map
therefore determines a morphism into that polycurve. The same
morphism rigidity holds for a target immersed in a semiabelian
variety, already after geometrically abelianizing both extensions.

Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, two maps
$f,g:X\to Y$ with equal geometric outer maps are equal in each of
these cases: $Y$ is a hyperbolic polycurve and $f$ has open image
on fundamental groups; or $Y$ is immersed in a semiabelian variety
and $C_{\pi_1(Y)}(f_*\pi_1(X))=1$. In particular a dominant map
from an irreducible reduced source into a hyperbolic polycurve is
rigid in this sense. These are Corollaries 1(b), 2(c)--(d), and 3
(149, section 1, manuscript pp.~11--15, scans 24--31; F5).
depends_on: A3, A5, A6; B1, B2; C4 exact homotopy/base-change comparison
notes: F5 surviving characteristic-zero Corollaries 1(b), 2(c)–(d), 3. Tower induction uses fibre extension pullbacks, not a global immersion. Also records withdrawn no-dominance assertion as ZAB7.

statement:
The full point-section theorem in positive characteristic — Let $K/\mathbb F_p$ be finitely generated. If a geometrically connected
finite-type $K$-scheme $X$ admits an immersion into a semiabelian variety,
then its $K$-points give distinct geometric conjugacy classes of sections,
already after abelianizing the full geometric \'etale fundamental group.
Thus both (*) and (**) of Theorem 3 remain injective with the full groups.
This proves the full-group assertion and the finite-field specialization
margin on scan 35 (149, section 1, manuscript p.~17; F7).
depends_on: B1; Lang finite étale isogeny; Stacks Lemmas 58.9.1 (0A48), 58.8.2 (09ZS)
notes: F7 full (*) and (**) are injective for the actual semiabelian-immersion hypothesis. Includes explicit reduction/spreading/special-fibre torsor.

statement:
What geometrically prime-to-$p$ abelianization loses — For $K/\mathbb F_p$ finitely generated and $G/K$ semiabelian, the kernel
of the prime-to-$p$ Kummer map on $G(K)$ is exactly $G(K)[p^\infty]$.
Consequently prime-to-$p$ (**) is false even for hyperbolic
once-punctured elliptic curves. Without hyperbolicity, prime-to-$p$ (*)
is false too. We retain the full arithmetic quotient $G_K$ and replace
only the geometric kernel by its maximal prime-to-$p$ quotient.
This decides the explicit assertion of scan 35 (149, section 1,
manuscript p.~17; F7).
depends_on: B1, B2; Kummer theory; Milne AV Tate/Abel comparison; AB_checks.py
notes: F7 prime-to-p (**) false already for an affine hyperbolic (1,1) curve. General (*) under only semiabelian immersion is false on an elliptic curve. Torus-immersed targets remain injective.

statement:
Nonabelian recovery for punctured genus-one curves — For $K/\mathbb F_p$ finitely generated and $Y=C\setminus D$ a smooth
geometrically connected genus-one curve with nonempty reduced finite
boundary, prime-to-$p$ (*) is injective. Thus every hyperbolic genus-one
type is covered, including B7 where (**) fails. This proves part of
the covering argument on scan 36 (149, section 1, manuscript p.~17; F7).
depends_on: B1, B7; multiplication-by-m covers; fixed-fibre lifting; generalized-Jacobian divisor equivalence
notes: F7 prime-to-p (*) is proved for every punctured genus-one curve over a field finitely generated over F_p. The common finite extension and preservation of p-primary order are explicit.

statement:
The remaining prime-to-$p$ point question — We have not settled prime-to-$p$ (*) for every hyperbolic curve over
a field finitely generated over $\mathbb F_p$, nor the implication
on scan 36 that compatible $p$-primary differences on all
prime-to-$p$ covers force equality. The remaining range in this work
consists of proper and affine genus at least two with
nonzero $p$-primary Jacobian differences. Genus zero and punctured
genus one are settled by B7--B8. B14--B15 additionally separate the
two specific genus-two pairs over $\mathbb F_3$ and $\mathbb F_5$
investigated below. The reduction proved here sends every collision
over a finitely generated field to a collision over a finite field,
with the same geometric genus and number of punctures. Thus the
remaining universal question reduces exactly to smooth proper curves
of genus at least two over finite fields; already its universal
genus-two case remains undecided in this work.
This retains the unresolved portion
of F7 (149, section 1, manuscript p.~17, scans 35--36).
depends_on: B7–B8; B14–B15; SGA1 XIII 4.0, Proposition 4.3, Examples 4.4, section 4.5.3; Stacks Tag09ZS; Milne AV III Proposition9.1 and Lemmas9.2–9.3 (geometric n=2, p odd); Saidi–Tamagawa2009 Remark1.2, Definition1.5, Proposition1.8, Corollary1.11(iii); Saidi–Tamagawa2017 Definitions1.1–1.4 and Theorem1.9; exact hyperplane norm identity and character descent; AB_checks.py
notes: F7 remains INCOMPLETE for the universal proper higher-genus finite-field prime-to-p point assertion, already in genus two. Every finitely generated-field collision specializes to a finite-field collision of the same curve type. B14–B15 separate both tested genus-two pairs. The fifteen odd-characteristic genus-two double-cover tests have unique compatible successful lifts in the connected degree16 cover Z of genus17. Their joint norm kernel K_2 is contained in J_Z[8] and contains pi^*J_C[8], isomorphic to (Z/4)^4. The actual point difference satisfies p^a[Qtilde-Ptilde] in K_2 when all tests succeed; no vanishing or point equality is inferred. Exceptional sets pull back under covers, and emptiness is equivalent to point injectivity over every finite constant extension. No hyperbolic nonabelian collision is claimed.

statement:
Marked field faithfulness in every characteristic — For any field $k$, the contravariant functor from finitely generated
field extensions of $k$ to their profinite \'etale fundamental groupoids
over $\Pi_k$ is faithful, where an isomorphism between two functors
must project to the identity natural transformation on $\Pi_k$.
In characteristic $p>0$ it remains faithful on replacing each geometric
kernel by its maximal prime-to-$p$ quotient and retaining the arithmetic
base groupoid. Thus the characteristic-$p$ margin to Theorem 2 is true
in this precise marked sense, in particular for finitely generated
extensions of $\mathbb F_p$ (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~10--11,
17, scans 22--23 and 36; F7).
depends_on: Kummer degree-one cohomology; normal proper divisors; base change to algebraic constant closure; purely inseparable invariance
notes: F7 Theorem2 holds for relatively marked groupoids, retaining the full arithmetic base. Frobenius and the forbidden unmarked conjugation are computed.

statement:
An affine hyperbolic polycurve need not immerse in a semiabelian variety — The semiabelian-immersion assertion on scan 26, repeated parenthetically
on scan 32, is false for the class of successive elementary hyperbolic
fibrations used in Corollary 1(b). There is a smooth affine hyperbolic
polycurve of dimension two every morphism from which to a semiabelian
variety contracts its curve fibres; this occurs even when both levels
have genus zero. This gives sweep rows ZAB1 and ZAB6 (149, section 1,
manuscript pp.~12, 15 and 17, scans 26, 32 and 36), including the
parenthetical claim that genus-zero fibres supply a global torus immersion.
B5 proves the stated corollaries without this assertion.
depends_on: Milne AV I.3.2 and I.1.5; explicit diagonal finite quotients; unit divisors; AB_checks.py
notes: Sweep ZAB1 and ZAB6. Gives examples with both levels genus2 and with both levels genus0. Every map to any semiabelian target contracts the fibre.

statement:
The field-map image, conservativity, and the limit groupoid — For a finitely generated field extension $L/F$, restriction
$G_L\to G_F$ has open image $G_{F_s}$, where $F_s$ is the relative
separable algebraic closure of $F$ in $L$. The map is injective
exactly when $L/F$ is algebraic, and is an isomorphism exactly when
$L/F$ is finite purely inseparable. Thus the field functor of
scans 5--6 is conservative in characteristic zero, and becomes
conservative after inverting finite purely inseparable extensions
in positive characteristic.
For an arbitrary field $F=\varinjlim F_i$, where $F_i$ runs through
its finitely generated prime-field subfields, the compatible
absolute groups satisfy $G_F\simeq\varprojlim G_{F_i}$; the analogous
statements hold for the profinite groupoids and their finite-cover
topoi. Keeping the whole pro-system retains the faithfulness of
B10, whereas taking only its limit does not. This closes sweep
row ZAB2 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~2--3, scans 5--8).
depends_on: Finite separable algebra descent; divisorial Kummer extension; pro-category Hom formula; B10
notes: Sweep ZAB2. All restriction and limit maps are typed. The marked pro-system is distinguished by a precise comparison from its inverse-limit groupoid.

statement:
Cofinal Artin models and the dimension of their groups — In characteristic zero every smooth integral variety has a dense
open which is a tower of affine smooth hyperbolic curves with
smooth proper compactifications and finite \'etale boundary.
Thus such opens are cofinal among models of a finitely generated
field, and their full geometric groups are successive extensions
of nonabelian free profinite groups. A tower of length $n$ has
$\ell$-cohomological dimension exactly $n$ for every prime.
This closes the additional assertions on scans 10--13, sweep
row ZAB3 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~4--6).
depends_on: Projection to a transcendence basis; spreading smooth curves and boundary; C4; A3; Serre finite-index theorem; Hochschild–Serre and Shapiro
notes: Sweep ZAB3. Cofinal smooth affine hyperbolic Artin towers and exact cd_l of their geometric groups, including the lower bound.

statement:
Reconstruction of a centerless extension and uniqueness of lifted maps — For a profinite extension $1\to P\to E\to\Gamma\to1$ with
$Z(P)=1$, the outer action determines the extension, with its
identified kernel and quotient, by
\[
 E\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\
 \operatorname{Aut}(P)\times_{\operatorname{Out}(P)}\Gamma,
 \qquad e\longmapsto(\operatorname{int}(e)|_P,\bar e).
\]
Use the compact-open topology on continuous automorphisms and the
quotient topology on outer automorphisms; the displayed pullback
is profinite because it is isomorphic to $E$.
If two extension maps over $\Gamma$ restrict to the same map
$P\to P'$, and its image has trivial centralizer in $P'$, the
extension maps are equal. Conversely a continuous homomorphism
$\varphi:P\to P'$ whose class modulo target inner automorphisms
commutes with the two outer $\Gamma$-actions, and whose image has
trivial centralizer in $P'$, extends uniquely to a continuous
homomorphism $E\to E'$ over $\Gamma$. These are the formal claims of scans
16--20 and 29, sweep row ZAB4 (149, section 1, manuscript pp.~7--9,
14). They do not require $\operatorname{Aut}(P)$ itself to be
profinite for an arbitrary infinitely generated $P$.
depends_on: Compact-open topology; centerless pullback reconstruction; direct conjugation computation
notes: Sweep ZAB4. Gives the actual extension isomorphism and uniqueness of lifted homomorphisms. Does not call Aut(P) profinite for arbitrary infinite-rank P.

statement:
The semiabelian Albanese homology claim for arbitrary reduced sources — For a general reduced connected finite-type scheme, a universal
semiabelian recipient of pointed morphisms need not have the same
$\ell$-adic $H_1$. Thus the assertion numbered 3 on scan 25 does not
justify Corollary 1(a) in all of its stated source generality.
B3 supplies a proof in that generality. This is sweep row ZAB5
(149, section 1, manuscript p.~12, scan 25).
depends_on: Explicit nodal normalization; complex finite-cover comparison; cyclic chain covers; AB_checks.py
notes: Sweep ZAB5. The pointed semiabelian recipient is zero for the nodal rational cubic, whereas H1 is Z_l. B3 avoids the failed comparison.

statement:
The toric-kernel disjointness assertion on scan 38 — Let $Y=C\setminus D$ be a smooth hyperbolic curve over an algebraically
closed field of characteristic zero, and let $J_D\to J_C$ be its
compact-Jacobian quotient. For $g(C)\geq1$, every nonzero
$u\in\ker(J_D\to J_C)$ satisfies
$(\alpha(Y)+u)\cap\alpha(Y)=\varnothing$.
This assertion is false for genus zero. There, for any nonidentity
translation, the intersection has at most one geometric point, and
its existence is determined by the equations below. This corrects
the bracketed claim and the margin ``$g\geq2$?'' on scan 38,
sweep row ZAB8 (149, section 1, manuscript p.~18).
depends_on: Explicit generalized Abel coordinates; degree-one function criterion; AB_checks.py
notes: Sweep ZAB8. Positive-genus disjointness proved for nonzero toric-kernel translations; genus-zero intersections classified exactly.
